title: Raga Bairari
hook: a short raga whose first hymn tells the mind to listen to a story that can't be told

segments.voice: Yesterday, listening in Todi: maaee charan gur meethe, mother, the Guru's feet are sweet. Your line was tender words. What small good thing did you tell someone close? Day one thousand ninety.

Small things can shine brightest in a room. A candle flame hides under a cupped hand, yet in the dark, eyes go straight to it. Some sections of the Guru Granth Sahib run on for page after page. Today's is not one of them. Raga Bairari is short, short enough to read in one sitting, and it comes right after Todi. But small doesn't mean dim. Its very first hymn opens with a command to the mind and a subject bigger than any book. Today: Raga Bairari, small and bright.
screen: `A CANDLE FLAME IS SMALL.` → `SHORT ENOUGH FOR ONE SITTING.` → `SMALL DOESN'T MEAN DIM.`

segments.voice: Bairari's hymns come from Guru Ram Das, mahala four, with Guru Arjan's voice there too. The first one opens: sun man, akath katha har naam. Sun: listen. Man: mind, the restless inner voice the Gurus talk to again and again. Akath: what can't be spoken. Katha: a story, a telling. Har naam: the Lord's Name. So, in paraphrase: listen, mind, to the untellable story of the Lord's Name. Stop on that phrase. Akath katha. An untellable telling. A story no one can finish saying, and yet the hymn asks you to listen to it. That's the brightness inside a small raga. The section is short, but what it points to has no edge. The hymn goes on, in paraphrase: through the Guru's teaching, meditate on the Lord, and peace and every kind of good will come. Notice that the first word is not sing, or bow, or give. It's listen. The mind is told to stop talking and take something in. That fits a small raga well. A short section is easy to hear whole, start to finish, the way you can't hear a long one in a single sitting. Tomorrow we'll do exactly that. Today, just the door into it: one word, sun, listen, and a story that can't be told. Small, because the pages are few. Bright, because of what they hold. Today's line: small and bright.
screen: `SUN MAN: LISTEN, MIND.` · `AKATH KATHA: THE UNTELLABLE STORY.` · `THE FIRST WORD IS LISTEN.` · `FEW PAGES, NO EDGE.` · then, large: `SMALL AND BRIGHT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: listen to Bairari, and let the mind be told to listen. If you can, play a shabad sung in Raga Bairari first. Then sit. Say the first two words of the hymn to yourself, sun man, listen, mind, and then do it. Stop rehearsing, stop planning, and just take in whatever is here: the sounds, the breath, the stillness under them. When the inner voice starts talking again, say sun man once more, gently, and go back to listening. If you pray, you can let Waheguru be the one word you listen for. The bell holds the time.
Raga Bairari. The short section after Todi, whose first hymn says sun man, listen, mind, to the untellable story of the Lord's Name. Today's word.
Your line: small and bright. Find one small thing today, a cup, a leaf, a kind sentence, and give it your full attention for as long as it takes to really see it. Day one thousand ninety.

howItsDone: Shabads from the short Bairari section of the Guru Granth Sahib are sung in Raga Bairari in kirtan, and because the section is brief, a reader can go through all of it in one sitting.
